- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +1.00 or +0.67) followed by a spike in news volume, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., -1.00 or -0.33) with high news volume, model underreacts — increase forecast by 3–7% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.00–0.33) — add 2–5% bias to forecast in such regimes.
- When sentiment changes direction abruptly (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- In high-news-volume periods, model often overfits short-term volatility — smooth 3–5 day moving average to reduce noise and avoid overcorrection.
- If true price rises >10% from prior 30d average, model often fails to capture momentum — apply 1.5x momentum multiplier to forecast if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days with no news spikes, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is negative and price is rising (contrarian signal), model often ignores — increase forecast by 3–6% to account for potential reversal.
